is heavily autobiographical, but such speculation must be qualified by the implication of
lines 45–6, which are taken (as Chernaik 80–1 suggests) from Sophocles’s famous Chorus
deploring human adversity in Oedipus at Colonus (1239–44): ‘Meanwhile this wretched
man, not I alone — as some northern shore struck by waves in winter is shaken on all sides —
so him too on the shore the terrible ruinous breakers continually shake’. This reference
